prize_parts.citation: For establishing liquid-liquid phase separation as a principle of intracellular organisation through biomolecular condensates

statement.case_for: Biomolecular condensates replaced the picture of the cell as membrane-bound compartments plus diffuse solution with a physical-chemical one: multivalent interactions, phase boundaries, interfacial tension and tunable material properties generate membraneless organisation. Hyman and Brangwynne showed P granules and the nucleolus behave as liquids, and Rosen's reconstituted multivalent systems showed that phase behaviour follows from molecular valency. This is a general concept of molecular organisation, not a single system or tool, and it is thermodynamics at work in biology. It has also reorganised how disease-linked aggregation, including the liquid-to-solid transitions seen in neurodegeneration, is studied. After about fifteen years the core idea is replicated across many systems and recognition seems timely.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection is that in vivo condensates are not always demonstrably equilibrium phase-separated systems, and the term is sometimes used loosely for any punctate assembly. Functional consequences are shown for fewer cases than the concept's reach suggests. A three-person limit also leaves out Pappu and Mittag, whose sticker-and-spacer framework supplies much of the quantitative physical-chemical content, and the category could be read as cell biology rather than chemistry. By contrast B026 is a clear chemical invention with an actual medicinal outcome.

responses.point: Aili ranked targeted protein degradation first as a new modality that turns protein removal into a designable chemical reaction, with the concept reproduced in many labs.
responses.response: I agree the modality is real and that it is the most broadly supported candidate in the opening ballots, and I ranked it fourth myself. My reservation is that the chemical principle (induced proximity through a ternary complex) is mature but the therapeutic proof is not, since no PROTAC has been approved, whereas condensates are validated at the level of concept. I would like you to say whether the prize should credit PROTACs and glues as one discovery or two, because the Handa cereblon work is mechanistically distinct from the Crews and Deshaies concept.

responses.point: Aqvist placed PROTACs and glues first because degrading rather than inhibiting a target is a simple, elegant idea with real consequences, which meets his game-changer standard.
responses.response: I accept the game-changer criterion and the elegance, but I read the criterion as satisfied by condensates too, because they changed how a whole discipline asks where and how molecules are organised. Where I disagree is on attribution: you keep the concept founders plus the glue mechanism, but that spans two mechanistic stories. Condensates have a cleaner attribution core in Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen, even if Pappu and Mittag are left out.

responses.point: Linke, as chair, ranked massively parallel sequencing first because its chemistry reduced the cost of reading DNA by orders of magnitude and its impact is mature and arguably overdue.
responses.response: I take the maturity and impact argument seriously and I do not dismiss sequencing, but I question whether scale of impact alone should decide a Chemistry prize. The chemical invention is the reversible-terminator step, and your own note shows that credit is split with Rothberg, Mayer and Ju, so a two-person prize is contestable. I would put the greater uncertainty on attribution there than on field fit for condensates.

responses.point: Brzezinski ranked long-range electron transfer through proteins first because the physical mechanism is stated quantitatively and tested by time-resolved kinetics on engineered metalloproteins.
responses.response: This is the candidate closest to my own preference for physical explanation, and the clean two-person attribution to Gray and Winkler is a real advantage. My question is the one you raise yourself: Marcus has already been recognised for electron-transfer theory, so how much of the protein-specific story remains uncredited, and does Dutton and Moser's work on natural systems weaken a Gray and Winkler-only prize? I keep it as an alternative rather than my first choice because I think the committee will find condensates broader.

responses.point: Somfai ranked Pd-catalysed C-N coupling first as a general, ligand-controlled method whose impact in pharmaceuticals is broad and whose timing follows the 2010 C-C coupling prize.
responses.response: Your attribution case is the cleanest on the list, with Buchwald and Hartwig independent and equal. I do not share the weighting, though: a methods prize in synthesis has a high and lasting impact but a lower conceptual novelty than a new principle of organisation, and a near-continuation of the 2010 prize may prove harder to explain. I do not rank it above condensates but I will not oppose it if the committee seeks a synthetic-chemistry anchor.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts condensates as chemistry rather than biology, and whether the three-person limit can fairly omit Pappu and Mittag.
How far in vivo condensates are thermodynamic phase separation rather than other assemblies.
Whether the PROTAC and glue lines should be a single prize or split, and the maturity of clinical proof for B026.
I have not verified details of the field histories and rely on recall.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for any shortlisted candidate. I am a Lund colleague of Heiner Linke and Peter Somfai, which is institutional, not a connection to any candidate. My field is soft matter, so I may weight B031 favourably.
